nodes.label: Read This First — Critical Success Factors
nodes.norm_label: read this first — critical success factors

nodes.label: Gamification System
nodes.rationale: Daily engagement is the core retention lever (target >40% first-week DAU). XP, streaks and badges exist to make a subscription habit-forming, not as decoration.

nodes.label: XP Award Formula
nodes.rationale: Base 10 XP + duration bonus + streak multiplier. The streak multiplier is what couples reward to consistency rather than to single heroic sessions.

nodes.label: Streak Tracking
nodes.rationale: Streak increments only if >24h since last workout, so a single day cannot be farmed for multiple increments. Requires storing streak_last_workout_date, not just a counter.

nodes.label: Achievement Unlock Conditions
nodes.rationale: Conditions are a closed enum (FIRST_WORKOUT, STREAK_7, STREAK_30, XP_100, XP_500, COMPLETE_ROUTINE, CHALLENGE_WIN) so unlock checks stay a pure function over user state, testable without a DB.

nodes.label: Social Challenges (Retos)
nodes.rationale: Named as a key differentiator vs generic fitness apps. Competition against other people is the social loop that pure solo tracking lacks.

nodes.label: Real-time Leaderboard
nodes.rationale: Rankings must reorder instantly when a rival finishes; polling would feel dead and burn mobile battery. Uses a Supabase channel per challenge.

nodes.label: AI Posture Feedback
nodes.rationale: Deliberately async (202 Accepted + polling), not real-time: MVP extracts 3-5 keyframes and sends them to Vision rather than streaming video, which keeps cost and latency bounded.

nodes.label: Subscription Monetization
nodes.rationale: Video feedback is the paywalled feature because it carries real marginal cost (OpenAI + Cloudinary). Free tier keeps routine browsing to preserve top-of-funnel.

nodes.label: Two-Sided Roles (User / Trainer)
nodes.rationale: A single users table with a role enum rather than separate tables: trainers are a superset of users, so every trainer must still be able to train.

nodes.label: API Response Envelope
nodes.rationale: Every response is { data, status, message?, timestamp }. A uniform shape lets the mobile fetch wrapper and React Query handle success/error without per-endpoint special cases.

nodes.label: Zod Validation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Validation happens at the API boundary before the DB is touched, so Prisma never sees unvalidated input and types are trustworthy past that line.

nodes.label: Clerk Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: Clerk owns identity; the DB holds a mirror row keyed by clerk_id, synced via webhook. Avoids storing credentials and keeps the mobile SDK's token refresh transparent.

nodes.label: Webhook Signature Verification
nodes.rationale: Stripe and Clerk webhooks are unauthenticated public endpoints that mutate subscription state and create users. Without signature verification anyone could grant themselves a paid plan.

nodes.label: Cloudinary Video Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Mobile uploads direct to Cloudinary with a signed URL, so video bytes never transit the Vercel serverless function (which has body-size and duration limits).

nodes.label: Keyframe Extraction
nodes.rationale: Cloudinary transformation URLs produce 3-5 stills from the video; Vision analyzes images, not video, so this is the bridge between the two services.

nodes.label: Supabase Realtime Channels
nodes.rationale: Subscriptions, not polling, and unsubscribe on cleanup. A leaked channel on a mobile tab switch drains battery and leaks memory across screen mounts.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrations Only
nodes.rationale: Schema changes go through migrations, never hand-edited SQL, so the checked-in schema is always the source of truth and environments cannot drift.

nodes.label: pnpm Monorepo Workspace
nodes.rationale: backend, mobile and shared live in one repo so domain types and Zod validators are written once and cannot drift between client and server.

nodes.label: Shared Domain Types
nodes.rationale: The mobile app's API response types are the same objects the backend returns. A single package removes the hand-sync step that normally rots.

nodes.label: Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Primary #FF6B35, 4px spacing scale, 8px radius, Inter. Defined twice (mobile constants + web CSS) because RN cannot consume CSS variables; the duplication is deliberate and must stay in sync.

nodes.label: Mobile Touch Constraints
nodes.rationale: Works at 320px width and touch targets >= 44px. 44px is the platform accessibility floor; below it, taps miss during a workout when hands are sweaty and the phone is on the floor.

nodes.label: TypeScript Strict, No Escape Hatches
nodes.rationale: No any, no @ts-ignore. The whole point of Prisma + Zod + shared types is an unbroken type chain; one any collapses it.

nodes.label: External Call Isolation
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Stripe and Cloudinary calls are wrapped in try-catch with user-facing errors. Third-party outages must degrade a feature, not 500 the whole request.

nodes.label: CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Lint, type-check and unit tests gate every push, so the strict-TypeScript and validator rules are enforced by machine rather than by review discipline.

nodes.label: Quick Start Setup
nodes.rationale: Documents .env.local for both apps. Note: the Prisma CLI reads .env, not .env.local, so a DATABASE_URL placed only in .env.local will fail migrate/seed while Next.js still works.

nodes.label: Workspace Package Globs
nodes.rationale: Declares apps/* and packages/* as workspace members, which is what lets apps/backend depend on @truerep/shared by name instead of by relative path.
